title.narrative: Provision of Emergency Lifesaving Health Services for drought affected Vulnerable Populations in Rural locations of Baidoa District

description.narrative: ltpgtBaidoa District in Bay Region is facing a severe health emergency, compounded by recurrent droughts, localized flooding, and mass displacement. The fragile health system has been overwhelmed by outbreaks of diphtheria and measles, which have placed children at extreme risk. According to the Somali Ministry of Health (Dec 2025), more than 1,000 children have been infected with diphtheria and at least 50 have died, with children aged 5–15 most affected. In parallel, MSF reports that Bay Regional Hospital recorded 1,192 consultations, 976 admissions, and 18 deaths from suspected measles between January and November 2025, with 70% of cases among children under five and 95% of families reporting their children were not vaccinated. These outbreaks underscore the urgent need for expanded health services and vaccination coverage in Baidoa’s rural villages.ltbrgtTo respond, SAMA proposes a 10 month Health intervention targeting 7 drought affected rural villages namely Barhanooy, Labatunjerow, Geldheere, Lowiile, Ismoodnoy, El-adow, Bulo-Sagar ltspangtin Baidoa District, directly benefiting 17,280 people with tailored support for the most vulnerable. The project will expand access to life saving primary health care through static facilities and mobile services, ensuring coverage for hard-to-reach communities. Outpatient consultations will be provided, including mental health support for individuals affected by trauma and stress. Pregnant women will receive regular antenatal care, with skilled attendants supporting safe deliveries, while health facilities will be strengthened to manage complicated pregnancies through caesarean sections. Referral systems will be reinforced to connect patients to specialized treatment across different levels of care.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtChildren under five will be prioritized through expanded immunization campaigns against measles and other vaccine preventable diseases, supported by reliable cold chain systems. Health facilities will be supplied with essential medicines and treatment courses to sustain delivery service. Outreach will extend to underserved villages through mobile medical teams, ensuring coverage in hard-to-reach areas, with health workers incentivized to maintain quality care.ltbrgtCapacity building will emphasize Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI), community case management, safeguarding, GBV referral pathways, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), ensuring that services are inclusive, responsive, and sensitive to protection concerns. To strengthen infection prevention and control, the target facility will be equipped with incinerators, handwashing basins, and institutional latrines, thereby enhancing the safety, hygiene, and quality of delivery service.ltbrgtThis intervention is aligned with SHF Strategic Objective 1 and Health Cluster priorities, delivering a coordinated, inclusive, and locally led health response. By addressing the immediate drivers of morbidity and mortality, the project will curb ongoing outbreaks, strengthen maternal and child health services, and restore dignity to communities in one of Somalia’s most underserved and high-risk districts. The project will be implemented for 10 months through 2 health facilities (ltbrgtLabatunjerow, Barhanooy Health Centres) and 1 mobile team targeting 5 outreach sites linked to the targeted health facilities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
